title: Orbit search equals split search
statement: For natural numbers $C,c$ and a binary word $w$, consider the search over indices $i$ from $0$ through $|w|$ for the first state that passes the round test, where the state at index $i$ is obtained by applying the search step $i$ times to the empty word. The resulting optional index equals the bounded search at length $|w|$ for the least $n\le |w|$ satisfying $n+C\cdot 2^{(n+1)^c}=|w|$, with failure returned if no such $n$ exists.
replaced: For all natural numbers $C, c$ and every word $w$, searching the indices $i \le |w|$ for the first round state (the $i$-fold iterate from the empty state) that passes the round test returns exactly the result of the exponential split search at length $|w|$.
